rail_guard.text: Fort William Station, halfway along the West Highland Line and all its scenic nonsense. It's been voted among the most beautiful railway journeys in the world, and the trains are very nearly on time.
Hop aboard! The Wildlore rail runs to every station you've visited in Great Britain. Where to?

fw_rescue.text: Ben Nevis is a big, kind hill with a bad temper in the mist. We go up in all weathers, so you don't have to.
The summit's covered in cloud about three days in four, and there's a cliff off the north side. Take a map, a torch and a plan. In that order.

fw_spotter.text: The Jacobite leaves here for Mallaig, a steam train that puffs along the viaduct at Glenfinnan, the one in the films. I've seen it go by seventy-three times.
I've never been on it. It's about the looking, you see. I look. The train does the rest.

fw_piper.text: I play the whistle in front of the shop. The pipers all have their own pitch and I don't argue with a piper.
The Ben Nevis Race is held every September. They run up and back down in about two hours. I'd take a bus. It's the same view, only drier.

fw_kid.text: I've climbed Ben Nevis, you know. Well, I've climbed the Pony Track a bit. It's very big. My legs said no.
My gran says on a clear day you can see Ireland from the top. She says that a lot. I think she just likes the idea.
